c144.title: A tech expo
c144.story: Last weekend, Anna helped her friend at a big tech [[expo]] in Kyiv. The [[keynote]] was given by a famous businesswoman who started as a [[product manager]]. Every [[sponsor]] hung a bright [[banner]] above its stand. At the door, a young [[promoter]] handed Anna a [[flyer]] about a new book. The book, about smart robots, was already a [[bestseller]]. At noon, the team sent a [[press release]] to all the news sites. In her talk, the businesswoman said she had worked in [[high-tech]] for twenty years. After the talk, Anna got a free [[poster]] of a smiling robot for her room. On the way home, she saw the same robot on a huge [[billboard]] by the road. That evening, Anna told Max she wanted a job in [[high tech]] one day.

c146.title: Uncle Oleh, the trader
c146.story: Anna's uncle Oleh works as a [[trader]] at a big bank in Kyiv. At Sunday lunch, Anna asked him what [[trading]] really is. "I buy and sell shares for people, a bit like a [[broker]]," he said. "You can open your own account at a [[brokerage]] with very little money." He showed her the stock market [[index]] on his phone. "This company pays me a [[dividend]] every quarter," he smiled. Then he admitted that he also bought some [[bitcoin]] last year. "Most people just try to follow the [[smart money]]," he added. He also explained oil [[futures]] and a strange [[derivative]] that nobody at the table understood. His old friend now runs a [[hedge fund]] abroad. "He started at a [[broker-dealer]], a firm that trades for clients and for itself," Oleh said. Anna laughed and said she would study [[asset management]], starting with her pocket money.

c148.title: The economy on TV
c148.story: Anna and Max were watching the evening news at Max's apartment. An [[economist]] in a blue jacket talked about a [[boom]] in online shopping. "But some small shops are close to [[collapse]]," she warned. Then she explained what a budget [[deficit]] is, using a simple chart. "Some countries owe more than a [[trillion]] dollars," she said. "When a country cannot pay its debts, we call it [[default]]," the economist continued. Next, a bank [[insider]] told reporters how criminals tried to hide their money. Thanks to good [[risk management]], the bank stopped them in time. Anna yawned and changed the channel to an ad for [[tax-free]] shopping at the airport. "I can't even imagine a [[million]] dollars," Max joked. "Airport shopping is the only economy I understand."

c149.title: A party for the rich
c149.story: Max's rich cousin Denys invited him to a [[cocktail party]] in a fancy hotel. The evening started with a funny old-style [[burlesque]] show with songs and jokes. Denys introduced Max to a [[self-made]] businessman from a small village. The man became a [[millionaire]] before he turned thirty. Next to him stood an oil [[magnate]] who owned a huge [[conglomerate]]. "I have [[business interests|business interest]] in five countries," he told Max proudly. A group of actors were discussing their new movie. "It did great at the [[box office]]," one actress said, eating [[caviar]] on tiny crackers. "Tomorrow's [[banquet]] is different, with a long dinner and speeches," she added. "And next month there's a charity [[gala]], the most elegant night of the year." Later, a quiet old man gave a big [[endowment]] to the university where Max studies. Max decided that was the most impressive thing he saw all night.

f01.title: Grandpa's coin collection
f01.story: On Sunday, Grandpa showed Anna and Taras his old box of money. First, he took out a shiny [[euro]] from a trip to Italy. "This is a British pound, also called [[sterling]]," he said. Next came an old French [[franc]] and a Danish [[krone]]. Taras found a red Chinese [[yuan]] note under the coins. Anna liked a Thai [[baht]] coin with a temple on it. Grandpa also had a Turkish [[lira]] and a [[dinar]] from Jordan. "A Kenyan [[shilling]] and a South African [[rand]]," Taras read slowly. At the bottom lay a Mexican [[peso]] and an old [[ruble]]. "Every coin has a story from my travels," Grandpa smiled. That evening, Anna and Taras started their own collection.
